title: Warning when dragging mouse in camera preview with camera positioned on the Z axis
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.8.dev6, 4.7.2.stable

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev6 - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 14 Sep 2026 22:41:30 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 2 monitors (1920x1080 @ 59.96 Hz, 2560x1440 @ 59.91 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (nvidia; 615.71.09) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13400F (16 threads) - 15.36 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When Camera Preview mode is on in a split view and the mouse is dragged inside that view, a warning is triggered if the camera sits on the Z axis.

>   WARNING: core/math/basis.cpp:1045 - Target and up vectors are colinear. This is not advised as it may cause unwanted rotation around local Z axis.

In 4.7.2.stable, this warning also comes with an error:

>  ERROR: scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp:495 - Condition "p.d == 0" is true. Returning: Point2()

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e302b91-7869-4c99-9d38-8abaf1e0d5d6

This only happens when the camera node is at `(0, 0, z)` where `z != 0`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a `Camera3D` node to the scene
2. Switch the 3D workspace to "2 Viewports" mode
3. Turn on "Preview" mode in the bottom view (split)
4. Switch to another tab and switch back (this is important for reproduction)
5. Make sure the camera node is not selected and drag the bottom view
    - Nothing happens. This is expected.
6. In the top view, move the camera node along the Z axis
7. Make sure the camera node is not selected and drag the bottom view
    - Warnings are printed.
